verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's AI Object Storage is a first-party, S3-compatible network store for training data, checkpoints, and model weights. Its buckets are managed independently of compute (via Console and Terraform), so data plausibly outlives any one GPU node pool. However, it is object storage reached over S3/LOTA, not an attachable volume or filesystem, and no evidence says explicitly that data persists after cluster or node teardown. missing for 10: an attachable persistent volume or shared filesystem (e.g., PVC/network file storage), explicit documentation of data persisting after instance/cluster teardown, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: Store training data, checkpoints, and model weights with efficient S3-compatible access directly to your GPU compute resources.
including CKS clusters, VPC networking, AI Object Storage policies and buckets, and Managed Inference resources
Training jobs that start with a warm cache can see a 30-50% faster first epoch compared to cold reads.
